patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and Microsoft Teams share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Fastmail only if your buying job matches “Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addre” rather than Microsoft Teams's shape. Choose Microsoft Teams only if your buying job matches “M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on ” rather than Fastmail's shape. Workflow advantage differs because Fastmail is shaped for Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom doma whereas Microsoft Teams is shaped for M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Pho. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and Microsoft Teams share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Fastmail is Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addresses — Business Basic from $3/user/month annual; a; Microsoft Teams is M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on — free Teams tier exists; Phone Standard ~$10/user.
- Company-size focus: Fastmail (micro, small-business) vs Microsoft Teams (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Researched limits: Fastmail — Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Microsoft Teams — Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job.

Limitations — Fastmail: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Shared addresses, shared calendars and the shared address book require Standard or above; Microsoft Teams: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job; Teams Phone requires an eligible Teams/M365 licence plus PSTN (PAYG or Calling Plan).

Poor-fit cases: Fastmail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications · Microsoft Teams is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job · Avoid Fastmail if you actually need Microsoft Teams's motion (M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telepho)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
